text:
Eric Robinson has a habit of scoring on Andrei Vasilevskiy. His third-period goal in Wednesday's 3-1 comeback over Tampa Bay gave him, as Cory Lavalette noted, "six goals in 18 career regular season games against" the Lightning goalie. It was his second straight game with a goal, after a shorthanded one against the Rangers.

The undrafted Princeton product and 2026 Cup winner has 12 points in 24 games in about 12 minutes a night, a pace well above our talent range of 1.46 to 2.26 points per 60. That pace has help. Carolina has scored 10.7 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and at five on five the Hurricanes are outchanced in his minutes (48% of expected goals) and far better without him. Evolving-Hockey noted last season that he plays with strong teammates, which flatters raw numbers.

What he brings is speed and pace: 94th percentile top speed, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 55% of his shots coming off the rush. He kills penalties and hits (45). Our numbers expect the points to cool; the role on a deep Carolina team is the part that holds.
headline: Eric Robinson, Vasilevskiy's problem
